summary: Discovery for Dedicated capacity: customer is a regulated mid-market bank evaluating reserved GPU pools for real-time LLM features. Key concerns: data isolation, burst/overage strategy, autoscaling behavior, SLA/latency targets, cost tradeoffs vs hosted. Agreed to run benchmarks with customer workload and exchange security docs.
topics: next steps: pricing, benchmarks, security artifacts
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, along with Priya and Jordan from our solutions team. How's the time for you folks?
00:06 Michael Torres: Yep good, thanks. We have about an hour. I'm Michael, head of ML at MapleGate. Sara and Ravi on as well.
00:12 Sara Lin: Hi all.
00:13 Ravi Patel: Hi.
00:20 Alex Chen: Great. The agenda  quick intro, understand your current infra and goals, deep dive on Dedicated (reserved GPUs), isolation, burst behavior, then next steps. Sound ok?
00:29 Michael Torres: Sounds good. To start high level, we're building a customer-facing summarization and assistant product. Latency important  sub 200ms for short responses, 2s for longer, but cost is a big factor. We're also in finance so isolation and auditability are required.
00:44 Priya Singh: Thanks. Can you talk through current stack and load patterns? e.g., qps, batch sizes, sequence lengths, and any peaks?
00:52 Michael Torres: Right now it's multi-tenant internal infra, K8s with GPUs. We're seeing around 30 qps baseline for the assistant, peaks to 120 qps during daily close windows. Typical sequence len 64 tokens for prompts, outputs around 80 tokens. We do some caching at app layer but want to move inference off our infra  ops burden and cryptic perf tuning.
01:12 Sara Lin: Also we need VPC isolation and customer data cannot leave our network except to vetted endpoints  that's the big restriction.
01:20 Alex Chen: Understood. Dedicated gives a reserved GPU pool that's logically isolated, plus we support VPC peering and private deployment options. For Dedicated we can do customer-dedicated nodes in cloud region with network controls  or if you need on-prem we offer our Private deployment.
01:36 Ravi Patel: When you say 'isolated', is that tenant isolation only or physical? We need strong audit logs, KMS integration, and can't have any co-mingled storage of raw data.
01:45 Priya Singh: Good q. Dedicated is compute-isolated  reserved GPUs and no other customers on that pool  storage and logs are configurable. We integrate KMS for key management and provide audit logs; we can also run a private control plane if you need totally customer-managed control plane (Private). Some early transcription notes: sometimes 'private control plane' gets misheard in the transcript.
02:03 Jordan Morales: Also worth calling out we can configure disk encryption, network egress rules, and retention policies  you choose retention windows for logs and metadata.
02:12 Michael Torres: Ok. On scaling: how does Dedicated handle bursts? We have spikes to 4x baseline for 30-45 minutes often. We want predictable tail latency and don't want to pay for idle capacity but also can't have dropped requests at peak.
02:25 Priya Singh: There are two knobs: reserved capacity (committed) and burst capacity. Reserved capacity gives predictable throughput; you commit to a number of GPU units. We offer burst pools which are shared across multiple Dedicated customers and can be configured with throttles and graceful degradation policies. You can also configure routing policies to fall back to a smaller model variant to preserve latency.
02:44 Sara Lin: Can you explain the graceful degradation? If we drop to a smaller model, how do we control quality checks?
02:50 Priya Singh: You control routing rules: percentage-based canary, lat-based, or cost-based. For example during a burst we can route non-critical routes to a quantized variant and keep critical ones on full model. We also support A/B rollouts and automatic rollback if response quality metrics degrade. We'll want to run evals against your prompts to set thresholds.
03:10 Michael Torres: What about cold start latency for the KV cache? We use a mix of long-running sessions and new sessions  KV warmup matters.
03:18 Jordan Morales: Our runtime uses continuous batching and KV cache sharding; cold starts are model and seq-length dependent. We recommend pinning hot models and pre-warming via a warmup traffic pattern; we can also persist KV cache across short-lived containers in Dedicated to reduce cold start. Expectation: warm requests similar to hosted ~50-120ms generation time per token depending on model.
03:38 Ravi Patel: SLA and uptime  what uptime guarantees and incident process? We need enterprise SLA for production.
03:44 Alex Chen: Dedicated comes with an SLA tier (99.9%+ depending on commit). For Private deployments we can negotiate different terms. We have on-call escalation, postmortems, and dedicated account support for enterprise customers. We'll include the SLA doc with specifics.
03:56 Michael Torres: For network, we need VPC peering and allowlist IPs. Also any egress to 3rd-party telemetry services is blocked.
04:05 Priya Singh: VPC peering and private endpoints are standard. We can provide static egress IPs for allowlisting. For telemetry we can disable external telemetry collection and ship logs to your S3 in your account.
04:16 Sara Lin: How are credentials and auth handled? SSO? RBAC?
04:20 Alex Chen: We support SSO/SAML, SCIM, fine-grained RBAC, and API keys. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your IdP and map roles.
04:28 Michael Torres: Great. Cost: can you give a ballpark  reserved GPUs vs hosted per token?
04:33 Alex Chen: Ballpark depends on model and utilization. Example: if you commit to an 8-GPU pool and hit 65% utilization on average, unit cost could be X per 1M tokens  I'll send a pricing worksheet with sample utilization bands. Hosted is higher per-token but lower ops. Dedicated becomes cheaper at scale but requires commit.
04:51 Michael Torres: For procurement we need a clear overage/burst pricing model and how autoscaling may cause unexpected bill spikes.
04:58 Priya Singh: We offer soft-burst with caps and alerting; you can set hard limits to prevent overage and have predictable overage rates. We'll document the overage repricing and cap configuration in the worksheet.
05:10 Michael Torres: Security review: Ravi will need SOC2 docs, network diagrams, key management procedures, and data flow for logs.
05:18 Ravi Patel: Yep and also encryption in transit and at rest proof, plus where backups live.
05:24 Jordan Morales: We'll share SOC2 docs, architecture diagram, KMS integration patterns, and a runbook for on-prem or private control plane options.
05:33 Michael Torres: Benchmarks  we'd like to run our workload. Can you support benching our model or do you only bench hosted models?
05:40 Priya Singh: We can run customer-provided models in Dedicated for benchmarking. We'll need a sample model file or container, and your dataset or trace for realistic qps. Priya: We'll coordinate the benchmark runbook after the call.
05:52 Sara Lin: Who owns the model updates and rollouts? We need change control because models affect behavior.
05:57 Alex Chen: Customers can pin model versions and control rollouts with canarying. We support automatic rollback on regressions measured by your eval prompts.
06:05 Michael Torres: Any constraints around proprietary models or licensing?
06:09 Priya Singh: We can host proprietary/custom models in Dedicated or Private. Licensing is per-customer; we will ensure images and weights are only accessible to your pool.
06:17 Ravi Patel: For compliance, can we run in an air-gapped environment?
06:20 Alex Chen: Yes  our Private on-prem option supports air-gapped installs; that requires additional professional services and licensing. We'll include that in the doc.
06:29 Michael Torres: Ok next steps recap?
06:32 Alex Chen: We'll: 1) send Dedicated pricing/worksheet and burst policy details, 2) share SOC2 and network diagrams, 3) schedule a benchmark run for your workload next week, 4) Sara/Ravi send qps traces and seq-length distribution. Anything to add?
06:45 Ravi Patel: Please include contact for security PM on Redwood side.
06:49 Alex Chen: Will do. Thanks everyone  we'll follow up via email with artifacts and calendar invite for the benchmark.
06:55 Michael Torres: Thanks all, bye.
06:57 Alex Chen: Bye.
notes: Transcript contains occasional ASR mis-labels and short mis-hearings (e.g., 'private control plane' sometimes mistranscribed). Call focused on Dedicated capacity and isolation requirements. Customer requested bench runs and security artifacts.
